install_startup.reason: The project's own compose file pulls ghcr.io/gitroomhq/postiz-app, with no Docker Hub equivalent (gitroomhq isn't on Docker Hub at all) - but the repo ships Dockerfile.dev, a real production build (pnpm install, pnpm build, nginx+pm2 to serve), just named for local/dev compose. Built from it directly instead (docker-compose.library.yml + Dockerfile.library), which needed two fixes: (1) Dockerfile.dev's apt-get for g++/make/python3-pip/nginx needs deb.debian.org, also blocked - switched the base image from node:22.20-bookworm-slim to the non-slim node:22.20-bookworm (already ships g++/make/python3) and got nginx by copying its binary + libs from the official nginx:stable-bookworm Docker Hub image (matched to the same Debian bookworm base for glibc compatibility, verified the copied binary actually runs before writing the Dockerfile). (2) the sandbox's proxy CA needed adding for pnpm install (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), confirmed working - pnpm resolved and downloaded 2200+ packages successfully. Both external-dependency blocks are genuinely resolved. The pnpm install itself is disk-heavy for this monorepo and didn't fit this sandbox's free space alongside the other unblocked apps' live containers - aborted at ~3.4GB free and dropping to avoid risking those, same call made for Cal.diy. Needs a re-run with more headroom - Dockerfile.library and docker-compose.library.yml are committed and ready.
install_startup.recipe_modification_note: Trimmed the project's own compose file to postiz + postiz-postgres + postiz-redis only (dropped Temporal/Elasticsearch/Spotlight - postiz only depends_on postgres+redis, Temporal is joined via a network reference, not a hard dependency). Built the app from Dockerfile.dev's own real production build instead of the ghcr.io image (see reason). JWT_SECRET/URLs left as the project's own documented example values (not real credentials).
install_startup.startup_command: docker compose -f docker-compose.library.yml build postiz && docker compose -f docker-compose.library.yml up -d
